name: Gilt market
summary: Gilt yields near multi-year highs after the 10-year rose above 5.35% on 16 Nov; a December rate rise is priced
state: The 10-year gilt yield rose above 5.35% on 16 Nov, its highest since 23 Oct, and the two-year passed 5%, a three-year high, as markets priced an 80% chance of a December Bank Rate rise after the Bank's first increase since 2023 (Trading Economics). The 10-year had risen above 5.3% on 13 Nov. Its monthly move is inside the 40bp line; Watch is kept because long yields remain near multi-decade highs.
for_you: Higher gilt yields feed through to fixed mortgage rates and government borrowing costs. Mortgage holders coming off fixed deals are the most exposed.
rubric_hit: Long gilt yields near multi-decade highs = Watch

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK gilt yields surge as rate hike expectations mount
Trading Economics — UK gilt yields climb on expectations of further BoE rate hikes

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
